source.title: Just Enough Shifts: Mitigating Over-Refusal in Aligned Language Models with Targeted Representation Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Mahavir Dabas; Si Chen; Charles Fleming; Ming Jin; Ruoxi Jia

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses refusal representations as a tool for its ACTOR training method and reports that method’s over-refusal results. It does not test the claim versions’ fine-tuning recipes, token-position KL, bypass interventions, safety localization, causes of shallowness, or deepening methods.
record.gate_note: ACTOR is designed to reduce false refusals on pseudo-harmful prompts and to preserve refusals on harmful prompts. Its post-training behavior is deliberately induced by its activation-based training objective; these results do not test whether the claim’s fine-tuning recipes or token-opening mechanisms erode safety. Table 1 outcomes are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. The paper cites other work on fine-tuning safety and refusal directions; those cited findings are not extracted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: ACTOR fine-tunes one layer with an activation loss, using a difference-in-means refusal direction, to reduce over-refusal on pseudo-harmful prompts. The reported results are the method's own compliance and AdvBench safety scores. The training data mixes harmful, benign and pseudo-harmful queries, and harmful queries are explicitly pushed toward refusal. So it is not harmful or benign fine-tuning of the kind V1/V2 describe. It reports no per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypass, localization test, causal account of shallowness, or deepening method. The safety degradation at high α is induced deliberately by the method's own objective.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that ACTOR reduces over-refusal across benchmarks while preserving harmful-query safety and general capability, and that it is data- and compute-efficient. Note that the reported '47.47%' average Compliance Rate gain is a relative increase.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation-target fine-tuning of a selected layer, with harmful, benign, and pseudo-harmful queries; it is not the harmful- or benign-instruction fine-tuning recipe in the claim’s original source.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that target-layer choice matters, that higher projection-multiplier values rapidly degrade safety, and that ACTOR’s target layer and best projection multiplier differ by model. It also reports results across different calibration budgets and training datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: ACTOR single-layer activation fine-tuning raises compliance on over-refusal benchmarks while AdvBench safety scores barely change (e.g. 99.62→99.03 for Llama-2-7b-chat).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation-targeted fine-tuning of one middle layer can reduce false refusals while largely preserving refusal of harmful queries.

fits_no_version.finding: Tuning layer 13 of Llama-2-7b-chat changes behaviour, while layers 5 or 25 leave it at default (Table 6). Larger α values rapidly degrade safety (Fig. 6), with no numbers in the text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal behaviour is adjustable mainly through one middle layer, and pushing activations away from the refusal direction can remove safety.

record.code_released: not stated (the paper says code is available but the link is absent from the supplied text)
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The reported compliance and safety outcomes are evaluated after training intentionally designed to produce those behaviors, so they do not establish the claim’s proposed safety-eroding mechanisms. The supplied text does not report uncertainty estimates for the main outcome tables.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-related results left out. The paper’s capability metrics, training-time comparison, layer-clustering scores, and comparisons of other methods were not extracted because they do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples to measure harmful compliance.
No ordinary benign fine-tuning without safety data. ACTOR's and SFT's training sets include harmful prompts trained toward refusal.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
Single-layer tuning and the layer ablation concern where over-refusal can be adjusted; no test of whether few weights carry safety.
No test of data or objective as the cause of shallowness.
No deepening method or test of its robustness.

record.verdict_notes: I agree with the reader's T4 / uses_without_test classification. Qi et al. 2023 (an original source) is cited only as the source of the HexPhi data. The Table 2 baseline comparisons, including SFT, are other methods compared with ACTOR and do not bear on V2, since the SFT data includes harmful prompts with reference answers.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test harmful-example fine-tuning that increases harmful compliance.
Does not test ordinary or carefully chosen benign instruction fine-tuning for harmful compliance; ACTOR uses activation-target training to mitigate pseudo-harmful false refusals.
No compliant-prefix, suffix, or decoding bypass test.
Fine-tuning one selected layer for ACTOR does not test whether a small set of weights carries safety behavior.
Does not test whether data or training objectives produce shallow safety.
Does not test training that deepens safety beyond initial response tokens.
